Theorem
[no local collapsing on a finite time interval] Source: cao-zhu 1. Theorem 3.3.2\group Cao–Zhu No Local Collapsing Theorem I Given any metric $g_{ij}$ on an $n$-dimensional compact manifold $M$. Let $g_{ij}(t)$ be the solution to the Ricci flow on $[0,T)$, with $T<+\infty $, starting at $g_{ij}$. Then there exist positive constants $\kappa $ and $\rho _0$ such that for any $t_0\in [0,T)$ and any point $x_0\in M$, the solution $g_{ij}(t)$ is $\kappa $-noncollapsed at $(x_0,t_0)$ on all scales less than $\rho _0$.

Proof
